_comment: Machine-checkable companion to docs/spec/error_code_audit.md. Maps every code in src/error_handling/registry.rs to the HGVS spec section it enforces. Tracking issue: fulcrumgenomics/ferro-hgvs#81 item L1. Follow-up gaps: fulcrumgenomics/ferro-hgvs#115. Tests in tests/error_code_audit.rs assert registry and fixture stay in sync.

_status_legend.enforced: Code reliably surfaces every input that violates the cited spec rule.
_status_legend.partial: Code surfaces a subset of violating inputs; gap noted in spec_section_notes.
_status_legend.registered: Code is present in src/error_handling/registry.rs and the ErrorType enum but no preprocessor or parser site emits it. The spec rule is unenforced at runtime.
_status_legend.missing: Code is documented in the audit but does not exist in the registry yet. (No rows currently use this status; reserved for audits where the registry should grow.)
_status_legend.infra: Infrastructure code (I/O, missing reference data); no spec section applies.

codes.description: InvalidAccession — accession does not match a recognized RefSeq/Ensembl/LRG prefix.
codes.spec_section: background/refseq.md (lines 45-57: NC_, NT_, NW_, NG_, NM_, NR_, NP_, LRG_)

codes.description: UnknownVariantType — coordinate-type prefix (g./c./n./r./p./m./o.) missing or invalid.
codes.spec_section: background/refseq.md (lines 64, 81-141); recommendations/general.md (lines 20-28)

codes.description: InvalidPosition — position is not a valid integer or offset position.
codes.spec_section: background/numbering.md (lines 16-28: c. numbering rules)

codes.description: InvalidEdit — edit type or format is invalid.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/{substitution,deletion,insertion,duplication,inversion,delins}.md

codes.description: UnexpectedEnd — input ended before description was complete.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/grammar.md (full grammar rules)

codes.description: UnexpectedChar — invalid character at this parser position.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/grammar.md; also catches retracted c.IVS notation per background/numbering.md line 32
codes.spec_section_notes: Generic UnexpectedChar is also raised for the retracted c.IVS notation; a dedicated code with an actionable hint is filed in #115 item 2.

codes.description: InvalidBase — invalid nucleotide base (must be A/C/G/T/U or IUPAC code).
codes.spec_section: background/standards.md (line 15: NC-IUB / IUBMB nucleotide codes)

codes.spec_section: background/standards.md — Amino Acid Descriptions (lines 210-214: IUPAC-IUB amino acid table)

codes.description: ReferenceNotFound — accession not present in loaded reference data.
codes.spec_section_notes: Infrastructure: depends on which reference set is loaded.

codes.description: SequenceNotFound — sequence data unavailable for accession with metadata.
codes.spec_section_notes: Infrastructure.

codes.description: ChromosomeNotFound — chromosome / contig not in reference.
codes.spec_section_notes: Infrastructure.

codes.description: TranscriptVersionNotExact — exact transcript version unavailable under strict resolution.
codes.spec_section_notes: Infrastructure: strict version-pinning policy, reference-state dependent.

codes.description: TranscriptSequenceUnreconstructable — cdot base synthesis cannot reconstruct a transcript whose CIGAR carries an insertion.
codes.spec_section_notes: Infrastructure: cdot data limitation (insertion bases not recorded), reference-state dependent.

codes.description: PositionOutOfBounds — position beyond the length of the reference sequence.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/general.md line 15: 'the reference sequence used must contain the residue(s) described to be changed'

codes.description: ReferenceMismatch — stated reference base does not match the actual reference.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/general.md line 15; recommendations/DNA/substitution.md (substitution semantics)

codes.description: InvalidRange — start > end or otherwise invalid coordinate range.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/general.md line 65: '_ (underscore) is used to indicate a range' (range semantics imply start <= end)

codes.description: ExonIntronBoundary — variant spans an exon/intron junction.
codes.spec_section: background/numbering.md (lines 21-28: intronic offsets per-side); recommendations/DNA/deletion.md (boundary cases)

codes.description: UtrCdsBoundary — variant spans the UTR/CDS boundary.
codes.spec_section: background/numbering.md (UTR uses -/* markers, CDS uses bare integers; boundary requires special handling)

codes.description: SelfCancellingAllele — overlapping del+dup pair within a single cis allele (e.g. 'c.[762_768del;767_774dup]').
codes.spec_section: recommendations/general.md line 58: 'descriptions removing part of a reference sequence and replacing it with part of the same sequence are not allowed'

codes.description: AlignmentGap — variant position falls strictly inside a transcript-genome CIGAR indel (a gap with no counterpart on the other axis).
codes.spec_section_notes: Infrastructure: a cdot transcript-genome alignment discrepancy (CIGAR indel), not an HGVS spec rule. Projecting through the gap would yield a silently-wrong coordinate, so it is refused.

codes.description: IntronicVariant — intronic variant cannot be normalized without genomic context.
codes.spec_section: background/numbering.md line 28: 'a coding DNA reference sequence does not contain intron sequences and can therefore not be used as a reference'

codes.description: UnsupportedVariant — variant type not supported for this operation.
codes.spec_section_notes: Implementation limit; surfaces incomplete coverage rather than a spec rule.

codes.description: ConversionFailed — coordinate conversion between reference systems failed.
codes.spec_section: background/refseq.md (cross-reference c./g./n./p. relations)

codes.description: NoOverlappingTranscript — no transcript overlaps the genomic position.
codes.spec_section_notes: Infrastructure: depends on transcript set loaded.

codes.description: IoError — file I/O failure.
codes.spec_section_notes: Infrastructure.

codes.description: JsonError — JSON parse failure.
codes.spec_section_notes: Infrastructure.

codes.description: LowercaseAminoAcid — 'val' instead of 'Val'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/protein/substitution.md; background/standards.md (3-letter code preferred); recommendations/general.md lines 41-43

codes.description: SingleLetterAminoAcid — 'V600E' instead of 'Val600Glu'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/general.md lines 41-43: 'three-letter amino acid code is preferred'; recommendations/protein/substitution.md

codes.description: LowercaseAccessionPrefix — 'nm_000088.3' instead of 'NM_000088.3'.
codes.spec_section: background/refseq.md lines 45-57 (accession prefixes shown in uppercase)

codes.description: MixedCaseEditType — 'Del' / 'INS' instead of 'del' / 'ins'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/general.md lines 87-104 (edit-type tokens shown in lowercase: del, ins, dup, inv, delins)
codes.spec_section_notes: Wired as InputPreprocessor Phase 6b1 via correct_edit_type_case_full (#268). Walks the input for case-insensitive edit-type tokens (del, ins, dup, inv, delins, con) anchored after a digit / ']' / ')' / '?' / '*' and lowercases them. Runs BEFORE Phase 6c (single-letter AA expansion) so 'p.Arg8_Lys10DEL' is lowercased to 'del' rather than mis-expanded to AspGluLeu. Lenient/silent mode emits W1004 and rewrites; strict rejects with E1004 InvalidEdit + hint. Closes #81 L2 follow-up to #264.

codes.description: WrongDashCharacter — en-dash / em-dash instead of ASCII '-'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/grammar.md (ASCII grammar); recommendations/general.md line 114 (minus sign semantics)

codes.description: WrongQuoteCharacter — smart quotes instead of ASCII '"'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/grammar.md (ASCII grammar)
codes.spec_section_notes: Emitted by correct_quote_characters in preprocessor Phase 3, so the warning fires when the input also contains valid HGVS syntax around the quotes. Standard HGVS does not use ASCII quotes inside any current production rule, so in practice the catch-all parse failure shadows W2002 for most realistic inputs.

codes.description: ExtraWhitespace — extraneous spaces in expression.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/grammar.md (no whitespace in production rules)

codes.description: InvalidUnicodeCharacter — generic non-ASCII character.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/grammar.md (ASCII grammar)
codes.spec_section_notes: Real coverage of non-ASCII inputs is via W2001 (en/em-dash) and W2002 (smart quotes). The generic catch-all is registered as ErrorType::InvalidUnicodeCharacter but no preprocessor or parser site emits it on its own — non-ASCII characters not matching the dash or quote correctors fall through to a generic parse error. Declared inert via `ErrorType::consults_error_config`, so an `--ignore`/`--reject` naming it draws a CLI diagnostic rather than silently doing nothing (#1196).

codes.description: MissingVersion — accession without '.N' version.
codes.spec_section: background/refseq.md line 20: 'variant descriptions lacking a version number are not valid'

codes.description: ProteinSubstitutionArrow — 'p.Val600>Glu' instead of 'p.Val600Glu'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/protein/substitution.md (no '>' at protein level)

codes.description: OldSubstitutionSyntax — 'c.100_102>ATG' instead of 'c.100_102delinsATG'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/substitution.md line 16: 'substitutions involving two or more consecutive nucleotides are described as deletion/insertion (delins) variants'
codes.spec_section_notes: Wired in the preprocessor (Phase 14) for the three deprecated multi-base substitution forms — c.79_80GC>TT, c.79GC>TT, c.100_102>ATG. Strict rejects with E1004 InvalidEdit + hint; lenient warns and rewrites to delins; silent rewrites without warning.

codes.description: OldAlleleFormat — '[c.100A>G;c.200C>T]' instead of 'c.[100A>G;200C>T]'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/alleles.md (allele bracket placement)

codes.description: TrailingAnnotation — 'c.459A>G (p.Lys153=)' annotations stripped.
codes.spec_section_notes: Defensive against ClinVar-style trailing protein annotations; tolerant input handling, not a spec rule.

codes.description: MissingCoordinatePrefix — 'NC_000001.11:12345A>G' missing 'g.'.
codes.spec_section: background/refseq.md line 64: 'It is mandatory to indicate the type of reference sequence file using a prefix'; recommendations/general.md lines 20-28

codes.description: DeprecatedStopCodonStar — retained for compatibility but no longer emitted: '*' is a spec-valid stop-codon glyph, accepted natively and canonicalized to 'Ter' by the parser (#1114).
codes.spec_section: recommendations/checklist.md:63 ('Ter or * should be used to indicate a translation stop codon; the X should not be used') — '*' is co-equal with 'Ter', not deprecated
codes.spec_section_notes: The '*' stop-codon glyph is spec-sanctioned (checklist.md:63), so correct_deprecated_protein_forms no longer detects it — the core parser accepts '*' natively as Ter and Display canonicalizes it. The ErrorType variant is retained (python-exposed) but never emitted. Reclassified from `enforced` to `registered` in #1114 (originally #125). Declared inert via `ErrorType::consults_error_config`, so an `--ignore`/`--reject` naming it draws a CLI diagnostic rather than silently doing nothing (#1196).

codes.description: DeprecatedStopCodonX — 'p.Arg97X' rewritten to 'p.Arg97Ter' ('X' is reserved for Xaa 'any amino acid', not for stop).
codes.spec_section: recommendations/checklist.md ('the X should not be used' for the translation stop codon); recommendations/protein/variant/substitution.md (canonical 'Ter')
codes.spec_section_notes: correct_deprecated_protein_forms in src/error_handling/corrections.rs returns ErrorType::DeprecatedStopCodonX; emitted by preprocessor Phase 6b (deprecated-form rewrites) in lenient/silent modes. Strict mode rejects the input. Closes #125.

codes.description: DeprecatedFrameshiftStar — retained for compatibility but no longer emitted: 'fs*N' is a spec-valid frameshift-termination glyph, accepted natively and canonicalized to 'fsTerN' by the parser (#1114).
codes.spec_section: recommendations/checklist.md:63 ('Ter or * should be used ... the X should not be used'); recommendations/protein/frameshift.md lists 'p.Arg97Profs*23' as a valid example — 'fs*N' is not deprecated
codes.spec_section_notes: The 'fs*N' glyph is spec-sanctioned, so correct_deprecated_protein_forms no longer detects it — the core parser accepts 'fs*N' natively as fsTerN and Display canonicalizes it. The ErrorType variant is retained (python-exposed) but never emitted. Reclassified from `enforced` to `registered` in #1114 (originally #125). Declared inert via `ErrorType::consults_error_config`, so an `--ignore`/`--reject` naming it draws a CLI diagnostic rather than silently doing nothing (#1196).

codes.description: DeprecatedFrameshiftX — 'p.Arg97fsX23' rewritten to 'p.Arg97fsTer23'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/protein/variant/frameshift.md (canonical 'fsTerN'; 'X' is not used for HGVS frameshift termination)
codes.spec_section_notes: correct_deprecated_protein_forms in src/error_handling/corrections.rs returns ErrorType::DeprecatedFrameshiftX; emitted by preprocessor Phase 6b (deprecated-form rewrites) in lenient/silent modes. Strict mode rejects the input. Closes #125.

codes.description: DelSizeSuffix — deletion described with a size-count suffix instead of a position range (e.g. 'g.123del6' instead of 'g.123_128del').
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/deletion.md: 'a deletion of more than one residue should mention the first and last residue deleted, e.g. NG_012232.1:g.123_128del and not NG_012232.1:g.123del6'
codes.spec_section_notes: Lenient mode emits the warning without rewriting (warn_accept) because synthesizing a safe end position requires offset/intronic semantics ferro does not infer at parse time; strict mode rejects. Wired in InputPreprocessor as Phase 13 via correct_del_size_suffix.

codes.description: EmptyDelinsInsert — deletion-insertion with empty inserted sequence (e.g. 'g.100_102delins' rewritten to 'g.100_102del').
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/delins.md: a delins whose inserted sequence is absent collapses to a plain del; #81 A3 canonicalization rule
codes.spec_section_notes: Lenient/silent rewrite delins -> del and warn once; strict rejects. Wired in InputPreprocessor as Phase 11 via correct_empty_delins.

codes.description: RedundantRepeatLabel — repeat description with redundant base label (e.g. 'r.100_102cug[4]' rewritten to 'r.100_102[4]').
codes.spec_section: recommendations/RNA/repeated.md: 'the format r.-125_-123cug[4], should not be used; it contains redundant information (-125_-123 and cug)'
codes.spec_section_notes: Lenient/silent strip the lowercase a/c/g/u label and warn once; strict rejects. Wired in InputPreprocessor as Phase 12 via correct_redundant_repeat_label, scoped to the r. description so subsequent non-r. descriptions are not affected.

codes.description: DeprecatedIvsNotation — retracted 'c.IVS<n>+offset' / 'n.IVS' / 'r.IVS' intronic notation.
codes.spec_section: background/numbering.md line 32: IVS notation is retracted in favour of the canonical c.<exon-pos>+<offset> form
codes.spec_section_notes: Cannot be auto-rewritten without genomic intron metadata (IVS number is not unique across transcripts). Registry uses always_reject(); the diagnostic carries E1006 UnexpectedChar + hint pointing at the canonical form. ErrorOverride::Accept lets a power-user opt out.

codes.description: DeprecatedConSyntax — '<pos>_<pos>con<source>' rewritten to '<pos>_<pos>delins<source>'.
codes.spec_section: SVD-WG009 (sequence conversion 'con' retired in favour of delins)
codes.spec_section_notes: Pre-parse rewrite in lenient/silent modes; strict rejects with E1004 InvalidEdit + hint. The legacy parser path still accepts NaEdit::Conversion for raw parse_hgvs callers; only parse_hgvs_with_config / lenient / silent / CLI go through the preprocessor phase.

codes.description: LengthMismatch — explicit reference sequence length does not match position range.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/general.md (range semantics: len(reference) == end - start + 1 for del/dup/inv/delins with explicit ref)
codes.spec_section_notes: Wired as InputPreprocessor Phase 13a via detect_length_mismatch. Lenient mode emits W3016 without rewriting (no safe auto-correction — either endpoint or the ref seq could be wrong); strict mode rejects with E1004 InvalidEdit. Detector handles g./c./n./m./o./r. ranges with simple integer endpoints; offset and *N/-N marker endpoints fall through (cannot compute length without provider). Covers del<ref>, dup<ref>, inv<ref>; delins<ins> is skipped (the inserted sequence is intentionally allowed to differ in length). Closes #81 K1 follow-up to #259.

codes.description: AlleleFractionAnnotation — trailing '[level=NN%]', '[heteroplasmy=NN%]', '[mosaic=NN%]', or '(NN%)' rejected with a targeted SVA diagnostic.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/substitution.md (mosaic '/' and chimeric '//' markers are presence-only; the spec carries no allele fraction in the HGVS string)
codes.spec_section_notes: Parser-level rejection at the trailing-content check in src/hgvs/parser/variant.rs::parse_variant. Closes the diagnostic gap left by issue #133 work-item 4 (allele-fraction soft-warning code follow-up, issue #278). Cannot be auto-corrected: the fraction belongs in accompanying metadata (VCF FORMAT/AF, ClinVar heteroplasmy field, etc.), not in the HGVS string. Not configurable: the rejection is raised by the grammar, which runs below the error-configuration layer, and there is no auto-correction to select, so every mode rejects. `ErrorType::consults_error_config` declares this and the CLI reports an `--ignore`/`--reject` naming it instead of accepting it silently (#1196).

codes.description: ClinVarProseMultiAllelic — ClinVar prose shorthand 'm.<pos><ref>><alt>/<alt2>' (bare-base RHS) rejected with a targeted SVA diagnostic pointing at the three spec-supported alternatives.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/substitution.md (mosaic '/' requires fully qualified RHS or the compact '<pos>=/<alt-edit>' form; the bare-base prose shape is not a spec form)
codes.spec_section_notes: Parser-level rejection in src/hgvs/parser/variant.rs::parse_phase_allele when the bare-base prose RHS is detected after the spec-compact fallback fails. Closes the diagnostic gap left by issue #133 work-item 4 (mosaic prose follow-up, issue #278). Not configurable for the same reason as W3017: raised by the grammar below the error-configuration layer with no auto-correction to select, so every mode rejects; declared inert via `ErrorType::consults_error_config` and reported by the CLI when an override names it (#1196).

codes.description: NonSpecMosaicForm — nested '/' + '//' at the same nesting level (chimeric-of-mosaic / mosaic-of-chimeric) AND the bracketed '[a/b]' / '[a//b]' mosaic group. Both are non-spec forms; one code family for two detectors.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/substitution.md (compact mosaic '=/<edit>' and chimeric '=//<edit>'); no nesting or '[a/b]' production is defined in HGVS v21.
codes.spec_section_notes: Always-reject (no canonical alternative exists, so no auto-correction). Two parser-level detectors in src/hgvs/parser/variant.rs: (A) `has_slash_inside_brackets` runs at the top of `parse_variant` and catches '[a/b]' / '[a//b]'; (B) the existing chunk-has-inner-slash guard inside `parse_phase_allele` upgrades to the same W3019 family. Both go through `non_spec_mosaic_form_error`, which inlines the spec-supported alternatives ([a;b] cis; acc:c.X/acc:c.Y mosaic; acc:c.X//acc:c.Y chimeric; compact =/<edit> and =//<edit>) in the message text so callers using plain `to_string()` see the migration path. Pinned by tests/issue_281_mosaic_chimeric_nesting.rs (closes #281, follow-up to #217 / #216). Not configurable for the same reason as W3017: raised by the grammar below the error-configuration layer with no auto-correction to select, so every mode rejects; declared inert via `ErrorType::consults_error_config` and reported by the CLI when an override names it (#1196).

codes.description: RnaThymineCanonicalized — 't'/'T' inside an r. (RNA) description rewritten to 'u'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/RNA/substitution.md and adjacent RNA edit pages (RNA alphabet is a/c/g/u; t is non-canonical)
codes.spec_section_notes: Pre-parse rewrite in lenient/silent modes via correct_rna_thymine in src/error_handling/corrections.rs; strict mode rejects with E1006 UnexpectedChar + hint. Closes the input-side loop on issue #232's deferred policy decision (closes #282). PR #293 / Display canonicalization handles the output side independently for raw parse_hgvs callers.

codes.description: ProteinBracketedAaInsertion — 'p.…ins[Ala;Pro]' rejected; canonical form is 'p.…insAlaPro'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/protein/variant/insertion.md (protein insertions concatenate 3-letter codes with no separator; brackets are reserved for variant-level alleles)
codes.spec_section_notes: Cannot be auto-rewritten because mixing 1-letter and 3-letter codes inside [...] is ambiguous. Strict / lenient / silent all reject with E1004 InvalidEdit + hint naming the canonical insAlaPro shape. detect_protein_bracketed_aa_insertion runs as InputPreprocessor Phase 17, and reject_protein_bracketed_aa_insertion runs as a pre-parse check inside parse_variant so the bare parse_hgvs path produces the same diagnostic. Closes #290 (follow-up to #248).

codes.description: InitiatorMetCanonicalization — a protein insertion (or affix-trimmed delins) whose canonical duplication form includes position 1 (the initiator methionine). The dup form is emitted with this advisory warning.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/general.md §3 (prioritization: dup preferred over ins); recommendations/protein/variant/deletion.md §63-65 (Met1-inclusive deletion); recommendations/protein/variant/substitution.md §45-65 (start-codon substitution rule p.0/p.0?/p.(Met1?))
codes.spec_section_notes: Emitted by try_protein_ins_to_dup / try_protein_delins_canonicalize in src/normalize/mod.rs when the resulting dup interval includes position 1. mode_behavior is `advisory` (WarnAndAccept in strict and lenient, Accept in silent): the warning describes ferro's own canonical output rather than a defect in the input — it also fires when the input already was a Met1-covering dup and nothing was rewritten — so no *mode* rejects it (strict would otherwise refuse ferro's own canonical output), and the runtime does not attempt to auto-correct the input to an alternative form. The emission is gated on `NormalizeConfig::should_warn_initiator_met_canonicalization`, so silent mode and `--ignore W3022` suppress it; an explicit `--reject W3022` is honored via `ErrorConfig::explicit_override` and promotes the advisory to an error, so neither override direction is inert. Before #1196 the push was unconditional and both were inert. Closes #92.

codes.description: DupSizeSuffix — duplication described with a size-count suffix instead of a position range, e.g. g.123dup6 instead of g.123_128dup.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/duplication.md (position range recommended; size-suffix form is legacy non-canonical)
codes.spec_section_notes: Detected by detect_dup_size_suffix in src/error_handling/corrections.rs. Wired as InputPreprocessor in Phase 13b. ferro cannot auto-synthesize the end position safely because g.123dup6 is ambiguous (could be g.123_128dup or g.124_129dup per spec Q&A). mode_behavior is warn_accept (Reject in strict, WarnAndAccept in lenient, Accept in silent) — a warning is emitted in lenient mode only (silent mode accepts without warning), and the input is not auto-corrected.

codes.description: DupExplicitSeq — duplication described with the explicit duplicated nucleotide sequence appended after dup, e.g. c.20_23dupTAGA instead of c.20_23dup.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/duplication.md (explicit sequence not recommended: longer, redundant, error-prone)
codes.spec_section_notes: Detected and rewritten by correct_dup_explicit_seq in src/error_handling/corrections.rs. Wired as InputPreprocessor in Phase 13c. mode_behavior is standard_correctable (Reject in strict, WarnAndRewrite in lenient, silently rewrite in silent) — ferro rewrites the explicit form to the canonical form in lenient/silent modes.

codes.description: DelExplicitSeq — deletion described with the explicit deleted nucleotide sequence appended after del, e.g. g.33344590_33344592delGAT instead of g.33344590_33344592del.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/deletion.md (explicit sequence not recommended: longer, redundant, error-prone)
codes.spec_section_notes: Detected and rewritten by correct_del_explicit_seq in src/error_handling/corrections.rs. Wired as InputPreprocessor in Phase 13d. mode_behavior is standard_correctable (Reject in strict, WarnAndRewrite in lenient, silently rewrite in silent) — ferro rewrites the explicit form to the canonical form in lenient/silent modes.

codes.description: NonConformantBracketCardinality — a standalone single-member allele bracket (c.[76A>C], g.[1000G>A], p.[=], c.[?], p.[(?)]). Allele brackets require ≥2 cis members or ≥2 trans groups; the canonical repair drops the redundant brackets.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/alleles.md (a single variant in brackets is invalid — 'c.[76A>C]' is misleading, use 'c.[76A>C];[76=]'; pure markers =/?/0 are valid only as a whole group inside a multi-group trans construct, never standalone)
codes.spec_section_notes: Applied post-parse on the AST in apply_bracket_cardinality_rule (src/hgvs/parser/mod.rs) — a top-level HgvsVariant::Allele with exactly one member is the uniform non-conformant signal across all seven coordinate systems (c/g/n/m/o/r/p). Strict rejects with a W3026 parse error; lenient unwraps the singleton to its sole member and emits W3026; silent unwraps without a warning. AlleleVariant::Display already renders a singleton bracket-free, so the corrected output is produced for free; the bare parse_hgvs path stays permissive and preserves the wrapper for programmatic callers (test_singleton_cis_allele_preserves_wrapper). Conformant multi-member brackets ([a;b], [a];[b]) pass through untouched. See #493.

codes.description: InsertionWithoutInsertedSequence — a bare 'ins' (an insertion with no inserted sequence), e.g. 'c.100_101ins'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/insertion.md:22 (the inserted_sequence is given as the nucleotides inserted, a range of the same reference sequence, or a range of another reference) plus docs/syntax.yaml dna.ins / protein.ins, neither of which has a payload-less production
codes.spec_section_notes: An insertion of nothing asserts no change, and the missing bases are not recoverable from the description, so there is no derivable repair: the registry uses always_reject() and strict / lenient / silent all reject with the dedicated W3027 code on the structured Diagnostic.code channel. detect_insertion_without_inserted_sequence runs as InputPreprocessor Phase 18, and reject_insertion_without_inserted_sequence runs as a pre-parse check inside parse_variant so the bare parse_hgvs path (which never reaches the preprocessor) produces the same diagnostic; the #1137 guard inside parse_insertion remains the structural backstop. Sibling class W3012 EmptyDelinsInsert is deliberately not swept up — a delins with no insert collapses to a plain del and therefore does have a canonical repair. Closes #1162 (diagnostics follow-up to #1137).

codes.description: AlignmentOnlySymbolInDescription — the description states one of background/standards.md's daggered 'used in alignment only' symbols, X (masked nucleotide) or - (gap of indeterminate length), e.g. 'g.10delinsX' or 'g.10delinsACGTX' — or, on the r. axis only, that row's lower-case RNA spelling x, e.g. 'r.10delinsacgux'.
codes.spec_section: background/standards.md:36-37 (the X† and -† rows of the DNA symbol table) with the dagger footnoted at :39 ('used in alignment only'), plus recommendations/general.md:48 ('nucleotides in CAPITALS using [IUPAC-IUBMB assigned nucleotide symbols]'), of which neither symbol is one. For the r. axis: background/standards.md:47-61 (the RNA symbol table — the DNA table's fifteen NON-daggered rows lowercased with u for t, listing neither daggered row) with recommendations/general.md:50 ('nucleotides in lower case using [IUPAC-IUBMB assigned nucleotide symbols]')
codes.spec_section_notes: The dagger is printed inside the symbol cell, so :39 annotates those two rows rather than competing with them; the decided rulings[alignment-only-symbol-in-a-description] rules that neither may appear in a description and ferro must refuse both. The stage follows the decided rulings[absolute-prohibition-enforcement-stage]: strict rejects at PARSE, via apply_alignment_only_symbol_rule in parse_hgvs_with_config (the same seam as W3026); lenient and silent accept at parse (lenient warns W3028, silent is quiet) and both then fail at NORMALIZE, unconditionally, in Normalizer::normalize_core_checked — because rule 1 of the README ruleset is about OUTPUT conformance, which no mode may trade. There is no auto-correction: X masks a base the alignment did not resolve. The check is AST-keyed on InsertedSequence::Named and never a scan of the rendered description, so XM_/XR_/XP_ accessions and intronic offsets inside an inserted position range (ins[244-8_249]) are not false positives. Note the symbol need not be alone — one stray X reclassifies an otherwise-literal run wholesale, so delinsACGTX / delinsXACGT / delinsACXGT are all this code. Closes #1627's standards.md:39 half. THE r. AXIS HALF RESTS ON A RULING (#1715): rulings[rna-axis-alignment-only-symbol-reach] asked whether the RNA symbol table plus general.md:50 exclude a lower-case x from an r. description the way :39 plus general.md:48 exclude an X from a DNA one, and was ruled on 2026-08-12: REFUSE, with standards.md:47-61 governing — the RNA table publishes fifteen symbols and stops, and general.md:50 names that tabulation as the source of an r. description's legal symbols. Measured on 2f4e3bb9 before the fix, r.10delinsacgux parsed to Named("acgux") and was accepted and re-emitted in all three modes with an EMPTY warning vector. The check is keyed on the SYMBOL x, never on the RNA alphabet as a closed set — an alphabet rule would reach Named("alu"), which is the separate unsettled question DNA/complex.md:169 raises. Lower-case x on a DNA axis (g./c./n./m.) is untouched, because general.md:48's CAPITALS makes it an ordinary name character. The uppercase spelling keeps its DNA citation and its N suggestion on every axis; the lower-case one cites general.md:50 and suggests n. A LONE or LEADING lower-case x never reaches the AST at all — parse_inserted_sequence dispatches on the first byte — so the grammar refuses it in every mode, exactly as it refuses -, and the two-stage schedule does not describe it.

codes.description: InsertionSizeCountWithoutSequence — the insertion states a COUNT of nucleotides where the inserted sequence belongs, e.g. 'c.5439_5440ins6' or its parenthesized spelling 'c.5439_5440ins(6)'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/checklist.md:32-33 ('do you provide the inserted sequence?' / 'Describing a variant as c.5439_5430ins6 is not allowed, the inserted sequence (for ins6, e.g., TGCCAT) should be specified', printed class="invalid"), with the axis clauses stating it constructively: recommendations/DNA/insertion.md:22 and recommendations/RNA/insertion.md:20 enumerate what an inserted sequence may be (the nucleotides inserted, a range of the same reference, a range of another reference) and neither list contains a bare count. recommendations/DNA/insertion.md:119 reaches the same verdict about a reported description ('ins24 does not define the sequence inserted')
codes.spec_section_notes: Sibling of W3011/W3023, which enforce the same numbered checklist item's :49 bullet for del/dup; before #1789 item 3 was enforced for del/dup and not for ins. The stage follows the decided rulings[absolute-prohibition-enforcement-stage], which names checklist.md:33 in its own clause list: strict rejects at PARSE, via apply_insertion_size_count_rule in parse_hgvs_with_config (the same seam as W3026/W3028/W4008); lenient and silent accept at parse (lenient warns W3029, silent is quiet) and both then fail at NORMALIZE, unconditionally, in Normalizer::normalize_core_checked — because rule 1 of the README ruleset is about OUTPUT conformance, which no mode may trade. That record measured this exact shape and predicted the outcome: the ins6 rows 'genuinely denote nothing' (denotation_of returns Denotation::Inexpressible and to_spdi refuses them by name) yet all three modes emitted them back byte-identically with an EMPTY warning vector — 'normalization is not impossible here, it is VACUOUS'. There is no auto-correction: ferro will not invent the bases, and re-spelling as insN[6] would assert they are unspecified rather than merely unwritten. Nothing is lost by refusing — when the NUMBER is known and the bases are not, the spec's own spelling is insN[6] (DNA/insertion.md:77) or insn[6] on r. (RNA/insertion.md:41, general.md:50), which ferro already accepts and which the diagnostic names. The check is AST-keyed on InsertedSequence::Count (src/hgvs/insertion_size_counts.rs), never a scan of the rendered description — c.849_850ins858_895 is also 'ins' followed by digits and is the sanctioned range form, and the two surface spellings ins6 and ins(6) reach the same node through different parser arms so a text scan would catch one and miss the other. TWO NEIGHBOURS ARE DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE. A count RANGE (ins(10_20)) is not this code: InsertedSequence::Range is ferro's node for both a count range and an uncertain POSITION range (g.?_?ins(23632682_23625413)_(23625324_23619334) is the latter, sanctioned by DNA/complex.md), so refusing the node would risk refusing a conformant description. And delins<number> is not this code: checklist.md:33 sits under item 3 'Insertions', and DNA/delins.md states no equivalent prohibition. inv<number> is a different shape again — NaEdit::Inversion carries an explicit length field, a range anchor already names both endpoints, and normalization drops the count, so no clause reaches it and no prohibited token is re-emitted. BLAST RADIUS, measured over the four committed corpora: 44 of 12,630,907 accession-bearing rows (39 unique strings) are newly refused, all of which were previously accepted and re-emitted verbatim. Closes #1789.

codes.description: SwappedPositions — 'c.200_100del' corrected to 'c.100_200del'.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/general.md line 65 (range semantics: start <= end implied by underscore range syntax)
codes.spec_section_notes: Wired as preprocessor Phase 15a via correct_swapped_positions. Lenient mode emits W4001 and rewrites c.200_100del -> c.100_200del. Endpoint tokenizer captures (main_axis, offset) sort keys per endpoint, so intronic offsets (c.100+5_99+3del), 3'UTR markers (c.*5_*1del), 5'UTR markers (c.-3_-5del), and cross-region swaps (c.5_-3del, c.*1_100del) are all detected and rewritten with offsets/markers preserved on each endpoint (#265). Closes #81 L2 follow-up to #264.

codes.description: SinglePositionRange — single-position range used where a single position is canonical (e.g. 'c.123_123del' rewritten to 'c.123del'; same for dup and inv).
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/deletion.md: 'position(s)_deleted should contain two different positions, e.g. 123_126 not 123_123'; analogous wording in recommendations/DNA/duplication.md and recommendations/DNA/inversion.md
codes.spec_section_notes: Lenient/silent collapse the redundant range and warn once; strict rejects. Wired in InputPreprocessor as Phase 10 via correct_single_position_range, covering del / dup / inv.

codes.description: PositionPastEnd — c. position lies past the resolved transcript's CDS-end (plain c.<N>) or transcript-end (c.*<N>) (e.g. 'c.946G>C' against an NM_ whose CDS is 945 bases). See #336.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/general.md: position numbering must reference an existing base; c.<N> where N exceeds CDS length does not name a base in the transcript
codes.spec_section_notes: Strict rejects via FerroError::InvalidCoordinates; lenient emits W4004 and short-circuits normalize() to the canonical variant (no further shifting); silent skips the check entirely. Wired in normalize_cds via check_cds_pos_past_end and in normalize_tx via check_tx_pos_past_end before each needs_normalization short-circuit, so substitutions and indels both get checked on both axes. Uses Transcript::cds_length()/utr3_length()/utr5_length() and sequence_length() so the bound source-of-truth lives in one place. Covers c.<N> against CDS length (bound_kind cds-end), c.*<N> against the post-CDS transcript suffix (transcript-end), c.-<N> against the 5'UTR length (5utr-start, #348), and n.<N> against full transcript length (transcript-end, #347). Intronic offsets remain out of scope.

codes.description: UnresolvableCentromere — a `cen` genomic position cannot be resolved to a concrete coordinate (a centromere is an assembly-annotated region, not a sequence-derivable base), so it cannot be normalized. `pter`/`qter` resolve to the first/last nucleotide and do normalize. See #488.
codes.spec_section: recommendations/general.md: `cen` indicates the centromere of a chromosome; `pter`/`qter` indicate the first/last nucleotide of a chromosome
codes.spec_section_notes: Emitted by normalize_genome when a genomic position is `cen`: pter resolves to base 1 and qter to the reference length (both normalize), but cen has no sequence-derivable coordinate. The NormalizationWarning::UnresolvableSpecialPosition is emitted unconditionally; strict mode promotes it to FerroError::InvalidCoordinates via should_reject_unresolvable_centromere(), while lenient/silent preserve the input. Mitochondrial/circular references intentionally do not resolve telomere markers (normalize_mt bails). c./n. telomere markers and cross-reference insert endpoints are out of scope (Phase 2/3).

codes.description: TranscriptFlankNotDescribable — pter/qter on a genomic-reference c. description (NG_/NC_/LRG_) denotes a 5'/3' transcript-flank position, not numberable in c. coordinates. See #488.
codes.spec_section: background/numbering.md: it is not allowed to describe variants in nucleotides beyond the boundaries of a transcript reference sequence; the flank-numbering proposal was rejected (consultation/open-issues.md)
codes.spec_section_notes: Emitted by normalize_cds when a c. variant whose accession has a genomic_context (NG/NC/LRG parent) carries a pter/qter marker. The NormalizationWarning::TranscriptFlankNotDescribable is emitted; strict mode promotes it to FerroError::InvalidCoordinates via should_reject_transcript_flank(), lenient/silent preserve the input. The genomic g. form is the spec-correct description for these positions.

codes.description: IntronicOnBareTranscript — an intronic offset (c.<N>±<M> / n.<N>±<M>) on a bare transcript reference (NM_/XM_ c. / NR_/XR_ n., or a bare LRG transcript LRG_<N>t<k> on either axis, with no NG_(…)/NC_(…) genomic context). The spec lists NM_004006.2:c.357+1G>A verbatim as 'not correct'. See #486.
codes.spec_section: background/refseq.md: a coding/non-coding DNA reference sequence does not contain introns and can not be used to describe variants in introns; intronic descriptions require a genomic reference sequence (NG_(NM_)/NC_(NM_)/LRG_199t1)
codes.spec_section_notes: Detected in normalize_with_diagnostics via intronic_on_bare_transcript_warning (HV::Cds with NM_/XM_ prefix or an LRG accession / HV::Tx with NR_/XR_ prefix or an LRG accession, genomic_context None, an intronic start/end position — including either endpoint of an uncertain-breakpoint Range boundary). Strict mode (and the errors-axis override) reject via should_reject_intronic_bare_transcript(), short-circuiting before normalization and escalating in normalize() to FerroError::IntronicVariant (the EINTRONIC tag in mutalyzer_map.rs); lenient emits W4007 and returns the existing value unchanged; silent accepts. Since #1630 the STRICT arm's input check also runs at PARSE, in apply_bare_transcript_intron_rule, where rulings[absolute-prohibition-enforcement-stage] puts an input-conformance check; the normalize rung is kept for callers arriving via the config-less parse_hgvs (#1632), and both read the clause through hgvs::bare_transcript_introns. The genomic-context form (NG_(NM_)) is the spec-correct description and is not flagged.

codes.description: NonCodingPositionOutsideTranscript — an n.-axis description states a -N position, e.g. 'NR_037639.1:n.-5A>G' (either endpoint of a range, and any allele member). THE -N HALF ONLY: n.*N is refused in every mode as E1003 InvalidPosition and never carries this code. background/numbering.md:52 numbers the non-coding DNA axis from the first to the last nucleotide of the reference sequence only. See #1748.
codes.spec_section: background/numbering.md:50-54 (the non-coding DNA reference sequences section): :52 'nucleotide numbering is n.1, n.2, n.3, ..., etc., from the first to the last nucleotide of the reference sequence'; :53 'nucleotides in introns are numbered as for coding DNA reference sequences (see above), although proceeded by n. (not c.)'; :54 'it is not allowed to describe variants in nucleotides beyond the boundaries of a transcript reference sequence, using that transcript reference sequence'. Also numbering.md:45, recording that the proposal to extend the numbering 'to specifically mark non-transcribed nucleotides' was rejected.
codes.spec_section_notes: THE ENUMERATION IS EXHAUSTIVE AND :53 IS WHAT MAKES ITS SILENCE AN EXCLUSION. :52 runs from the first nucleotide to the last and names no * zone and no negative one; on its own that could be terseness. :53 grants introns EXPLICITLY, so the spec knew how to add a zone to this axis and added exactly one. :54 then prohibits the nucleotide outright. THE ONE COUNTER-READING, AND WHY IT FAILS: :53 incorporates the coding numbering by reference ('see above') and the coding numbering is where -N and *N are defined, so it can look as though :53 pulls those zones onto n. too. It does not. The coding numbering (:18-:44) is three NAMED bullets — 'protein coding region' (:20), 'untranslated region (UTR)' (:28, where c.-1/c.*1 are defined) and 'introns' (:33) — and :53's subject is 'nucleotides IN INTRONS', so its 'see above' is scoped by its own sentence to the third; the -/* zones sit in the second, which it never reaches. The coding section's closing bullet confirms it, being :54's sentence verbatim: :43-:44 'transcript flanking'. So c.*1 and 'nothing beyond the boundary' coexist on c. precisely BECAUSE the UTR is inside the transcript; n. has no UTR bullet, so :54 stands unopposed there. THIS CODE IS THE -N HALF ONLY, AND THE SPLIT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. One clause reading covers both markers; the STAGES differ. Over ferro's four committed corpora (clinvar_hgvs_500k, clinvar_hgvs_unique, cmrg_genes_exhaustive, paraphase_genes_exhaustive) 0 of 103,762 n.-axis rows state *N, while 5 state -N: NR_003051.3:n.-57T>C, NR_003051.3:n.-30_-7dup and LRG_163t1:n.-5delins17 (all RMRP, whose upstream promoter variants are the clinically conventional case), NR_029595.1:n.-4771G>T (MIR208A) and NR_033294.1:n.-6G>A (SNORD118). Those are descriptions NCBI publishes today, so lenient and silent must keep accepting them and this code stays mode-gated. The zero for *N is a REAL zero and not a structural one — the same scan over the same rows finds -N five times — so n.*N is refused UNCONDITIONALLY as E1003 from parse_variant, at zero measured corpus cost. That unconditional arm is a MAINTAINER DECISION under rule 6 of the README ruleset, disclosed under rule 7 and REVISITABLE on user demand; it departs from rulings[absolute-prohibition-enforcement-stage], whose objection to unconditional refusal was that it would strand a caller round-tripping a real-world corpus — measurably empty here. The full record, including why the tempting 'it is a grammar matter, not a conformance one' scoping argument is NOT conclusive (checklist.md:16's g.*10 is exactly parallel and that record mode-gates it), is on src/hgvs/noncoding_zones.rs and pinned by tests/it/issue_1748_noncoding_axis_zones.rs. STAGE FOR THIS CODE: strict rejects at PARSE via apply_noncoding_zone_rule in parse_hgvs_with_config (the same seam as W3026 and W3028); lenient accepts and warns W4008; silent accepts quietly. NO AUTO-CORRECTION: re-expressing n.-5 as an in-transcript coordinate needs the transcript's length, which the parser does not hold, and :52 denies the zone rather than the spelling. MESSAGE SCOPING: :54's clause is conditioned on the transcript BEING the reference sequence ('using that transcript reference sequence'), so it is quoted only for a bare transcript. For the selector form NG_007485.1(NR_003529.3):n.-40000del the reference sequence is the genomic NG_007485.1, which does contain the nucleotide, and the refusal stands on :52 alone. THE CODING AXIS IS UNTOUCHED, including ferro's deliberate past-the-end c.* in the #797 poly-A carve-out. THE r. AXIS IS UNTOUCHED, DELIBERATELY AND NOT BY OMISSION: numbering.md:58 makes an r. description's numbering follow 'the associated CODING OR NON-CODING DNA reference sequence', so :61 makes r.*5 conformant on a coding reference and :60 makes it prohibited on a non-coding one. The zone set is a property of the REFERENCE and the parser holds no provider, so refusing at parse would refuse conformant descriptions. n. is decidable at parse for a reason that does not transfer — general.md:26 makes the prefix a claim about the reference TYPE ('n for a non-coding DNA reference sequence'), so :52 binds on the prefix alone. AST-KEYED on a negative TxPos.base, never a scan of the rendered text — an accession contains -, and so does :53's intronic offset. n.0 is NOT this code (E1003 InvalidPosition, refused at the grammar in every mode) and an offset is never this code whatever its sign (the -3 in n.6-3 is a distance from position 6, not a zone).

codes.description: GenomicPositionOffset — the description states a +/- offset on a genomic-family position (g., m. or o.), e.g. 'NC_000001.11:g.266+2del', 'NC_000001.11:g.266-268del' (checklist.md:45's hyphen-as-range, which the grammar reads as an offset) or 'NC_012920.1:m.100+2A>G'. Includes the +? / -? unknown-offset sentinels. See #1628 and #1630.
codes.spec_section: background/numbering.md:6, :8 and :11 — three consecutive bullets numbering the genomic, circular and mitochondrial axes, each ending 'Nucleotide numbers based on a ... reference sequence do not include "+", "-", "*", or other prefixes'. recommendations/checklist.md:16 states the same for g. ('genomic (g.) reference sequences start with nucleotide 1 and can not have nucleotides with additions like a +, -, or *'), and recommendations/checklist.md:45 marks the hyphen-as-range spelling 'Not correct'.
codes.spec_section_notes: THE CLAUSE IS STATED PER AXIS, THREE TIMES, so covering m. and o. is not a widening of a g.-only clause — refusing on g. alone would be the under-reading; numbering.md:9 additionally makes a mitochondrial reference 'a special circular genomic reference sequence', so m. would inherit :8 even without :11. An intronic c.100+2 is anchored to an exon boundary from the transcript's exon table; a genomic accession has none, so g.266+2 measures an offset from nothing and names no nucleotide. FERRO'S OWN CONVERSION LAYER ALREADY AGREED: hgvs_to_spdi (#1641) and the VCF writer (#1734) were each fixed to refuse rather than silently drop the offset, which had them return one triple for g.266+2del, g.266-268del and g.266del alike. STAGE: follows the decided rulings[absolute-prohibition-enforcement-stage] — strict rejects at PARSE via apply_genomic_offset_rule in parse_hgvs_with_config (the same seam as W3026, W3028 and W4008); lenient and silent accept at parse (lenient warns W4009, silent is quiet) and both then fail at NORMALIZE, unconditionally, in Normalizer::normalize_core_checked, because rule 1 of the README ruleset is about OUTPUT conformance and no mode may trade it. NO AUTO-CORRECTION, DELIBERATELY: dropping the offset answers for a different nucleotide (exactly the flattening #1641/#1734 were filed to stop), and rewriting g.266-268del as the range g.266_268del guesses a three-base deletion out of a one-base one. MEASURED ON 9fb126ba BEFORE THE FIX: all three modes accepted these at parse AND re-emitted them from normalize byte-identically with an EMPTY warning vector — normalization was not impossible, it was vacuous, which is worse because the output looks normalized. AST-KEYED on GenomePos::offset (src/hgvs/genomic_offsets.rs), never a scan of the rendered description, so an accession's digits and dots and a gene symbol's hyphen (NC_012920.1(MT-ND1):m.3460G>A) are not false positives. It walks BOTH endpoints of a complex (a_b) boundary, which the SPDI and VCF guards do not, since UncertainBoundary::inner() returns None for a Range. offset: Some(0) is not matched, because GenomePos::Display prints nothing for it and the position renders as a bare base. g.*10 and a leading g.-100 are refused by the GRAMMAR in every mode (no production matches) and never carry this code — that grammar accident is why checklist.md:16 read as one-third enforced. CORPUS COST: 8 of the spec corpus's 164 prohibited rows (4 checklist.md:16-genomic-has-no-offsets + 4 checklist.md:45-range-is-underscore), and 2 rows of 9,949,738 in the four committed real-world corpora. W4008 is held by NonCodingPositionOutsideTranscript, hence W4009.

codes.description: RefSeqMismatch — stated reference base mismatches actual reference (warning sibling of E3002).
codes.spec_section: recommendations/general.md line 15: 'the reference sequence used must contain the residue(s) described to be changed'
codes.spec_section_notes: Emitted as NormalizationWarning::RefSeqMismatch from src/normalize/mod.rs when validate_reference detects a mismatch during normalization. Coverage is partial because emission requires loaded reference data; without reference data (the common CLI case) parsing succeeds with no warning. With reference data the sibling error E3002 is raised in strict mode instead.

codes.description: OverlapConflictingEdits — two or more cis-allele edits share identical reference bounds (e.g. g.[100G>A;100A>C]).
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/alleles.md (cis-allele variant descriptions); recommendations/general.md line 15: 'the reference sequence used must contain the residue(s) described to be changed'
codes.spec_section_notes: Detected in src/normalize/overlap.rs by detect_overlap_conflicts and wired into normalize_allele after per-variant normalization. Variant output is preserved; the warning is advisory.

codes.description: VariantExceedsReference — the provider returned fewer bytes than the HGVS interval span; the variant references positions outside the reference (e.g. NG_032871.1:g.32476_53457delins... when the reference is shorter than position 53457).
codes.spec_section: background/refseq.md §43: 'the entirety of the variant sequence must be encompassed by the selected reference sequence'
codes.spec_section_notes: Emitted as NormalizationWarning::CanonicalSplitSkipped from apply_canonical_split in src/normalize/mod.rs when ref_bytes.len() != expected_span. Strict mode promotes to FerroError::VariantExceedsReference via Normalizer::normalize; lenient mode emits the warning and preserves input; silent mode preserves without warning. Matches biocommons hgvs which raises HGVSInvalidVariantError. Closes #355.

codes.description: IncompleteCdsStartReference — transcript has a 5′-incomplete CDS (Ensembl cds_start_NF); not an HGVS-recommended reference for c./p./r. description.
codes.spec_section: background/refseq.md (reference sequence requirements for coding/protein description)
codes.spec_section_notes: Detected at the top of normalize_cds / normalize_protein / normalize_rna (src/normalize/mod.rs) via a get_transcript lookup on the variant's own transcript accession: when Transcript::cds_start_incomplete is true, the coordinate is passed through UNCHANGED (no re-numbering) in every mode — only whether the NormalizationWarning::IncompleteCdsStartReference warning is pushed is mode-gated (should_warn_incomplete_cds_start() / should_reject_incomplete_cds_start()). Strict mode's should_reject_incomplete_cds_start() promotes the warning to FerroError::InvalidCoordinates in the normalize() wrapper; lenient warns and preserves; silent preserves without a warning. n. is unaffected (normalize_tx never consults this flag). Input-side counterpart to Task 4's projection-side c./p./r. decline (#972).

codes.description: MembersCoalescedFromReportedForm — normalization returned fewer cis members than the input described; two or more separately-reported variants merged into one (e.g. g.[100del;102_105del] normalizing to g.100_105delinsAC).
codes.spec_section: recommendations/DNA/delins.md:79-84: the coalesced form is the correct description, while "the two variants may have been reported (or might occur) individually" — provenance the normalized string cannot carry
codes.spec_section_notes: Emitted as NormalizationWarning::MembersCoalesced from the single normalization exit in src/normalize/mod.rs that compares cis_member_count(input) against cis_member_count(output), so every pass that can reduce the count is covered by one check. Purely informational: the normalized string is identical whether or not the warning is produced, and the warning never rejects or alters the result. Emission is unconditional and in every mode — there is no ErrorConfig consult site, which is why ErrorType::consults_error_config() declares it inert, so --ignore W5005 / --reject W5005 report themselves as having no effect rather than silently doing nothing (#2092). Registered in src/error_handling/registry.rs by #2092; before that the code was minted by ErrorType::code() but had no registry entry, so `ferro explain W5005` failed.

codes.description: MalformedRecord — a required GFF/GTF column failed to parse; the offending row is dropped.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 2.

codes.description: UnsupportedFormat — the input file cannot be classified as GFF3 or GTF. Reserved for future use.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 1.

codes.description: StrandRequired — a transcript with an unspecified or unknown strand is dropped.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 4.

codes.description: UnknownFormat — format could not be determined with high confidence; defaulted to GFF3.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 1.

codes.description: InlineFastaIgnored — a ##FASTA directive was encountered; inline sequences are not parsed. Reserved.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 2.

codes.description: OrphanFeature — a feature references a parent ID not present in the file; the orphan is dropped.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 3.

codes.description: TranscriptWithoutExons — a transcript-like feature has no exon, UTR, or CDS children; the transcript is dropped.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 4.

codes.description: GeneAsTranscript — a gene feature with direct CDS children (no mRNA/transcript) is treated as a transcript.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; prokaryotic GFF3 convention. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 4.

codes.description: PhaseAppliedToCdsStart — the leading CDS has a non-zero phase; cds_start_genomic was shifted by the phase value.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 4.

codes.description: PhaseUnavailable — the leading CDS has no phase recorded; the unshifted CDS start is used.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 4.

codes.description: StopCodonAssumed — no explicit stop_codon record found; cds_end_genomic was extended by 3 bp on the 3' side.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 4.

codes.description: ConflictingProteinId — CDS fragments of one transcript report disagreeing protein_id values; protein_id is left unset and the projector's transcript-id fallback applies.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 4.

codes.description: CdsLengthNotMod3 — FASTA validation found a CDS whose length is not divisible by 3. Reserved for Phase 4.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 5.

codes.description: NonCanonicalStartCodon — FASTA validation found the first CDS codon is not in {ATG, CTG, GTG, TTG}. Reserved for Phase 4.
codes.spec_section_notes: GFF/GTF loader infrastructure; no HGVS spec section applies. See GFF/GTF loader design §6 Stage 5.
